title: JuryGCN: Quantifying Jackknife Uncertainty on Graph Convolutional Networks

problem.claim: Existing GCN work largely prioritizes predictive accuracy while neglecting confidence and uncertainty in predictions.

gap.claim: Uncertainty quantification for GCN has been insufficiently studied, and existing approaches either lack deterministic quantification or modify GCN training through additional parameters or architectures.

contributions.claim: JuryGCN quantifies node uncertainty as the width of a confidence interval computed with a jackknife estimator.
Influence functions estimate changes in GCN parameters without retraining to improve computational scalability.
The approach performs deterministic uncertainty quantification without modifying the GCN architecture or adding parameters.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on real-world datasets covering active learning and semi-supervised node classification.
The authors report that the experiments demonstrate the efficacy of JuryGCN.

narrative_sequence.summary: GCNs show strong empirical performance in real-world applications.
Most GCN research emphasizes accuracy rather than prediction confidence or uncertainty.
Existing GCN uncertainty methods are scarce and have limitations involving determinism or training modifications.
JuryGCN uses jackknife confidence-interval widths for node uncertainty and influence functions for scalable parameter-change estimation.
Experiments assess the method on real-world datasets in active learning and semi-supervised node classification.

source_observation.claim: Uncertainty can be represented as the width of a confidence interval produced by a jackknife estimator.

interpretation.claim: A deterministic interval-width measure can provide node-level uncertainty without altering the base GCN architecture.

application.claim: Use confidence-interval widths as uncertainty signals for graph tasks such as active learning.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how the measure behaves across graph types, datasets, or tasks beyond the reported evaluation settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the exact jackknife estimator or confidence-interval construction.
The abstract does not report datasets, baselines, quantitative results, or computational costs.
The abstract does not establish theoretical guarantees or independent verification of efficacy.
